title: test-0007-MAT-LINEAREQ1
passage: An equation is a mathematical statement asserting that two expressions are equal. Unlike an expression, which is just a collection of numbers and variables, an equation must contain an equals sign. When we solve an equation, we find the value of the variable that makes the statement true. To keep the balance, whatever operation you perform on one side of the equation, you must perform the exact same operation on the other side. When moving a term from one side to the other, we use transposition, which requires changing the sign of that term. For example, to solve 4x - 7 = 13, we first add 7 to both sides to get 4x = 20. Then, we divide both sides by 4 to find x = 5. Remember that variables represent unknown numbers, not labels for objects. Furthermore, when dealing with brackets, a negative sign outside applies to every term inside. Finally, when solving word problems, always check if your answer makes sense in the real world; for instance, a number of people must be a whole number. If you find a negative result for a count of items, recheck your steps.
summary: To keep the balance, you must do the same operation on both sides of the equation. When moving a term from one side to the other, we use transposition, which requires changing the sign of that term.
